transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, it’s mostly when I get into a slow elevator or some small room where the door’s locked. Right away my chest kind of jumps, and I feel this strong urge to get back out before I can even think straight.
Do you ever have these episodes of sudden chest jumps and strong urges to escape in situations other than being in small or locked spaces?
No, not really. It’s pretty much when I’m in a slow elevator or a small room where the door’s locked. That’s when it hits right away—my chest jumps and I just feel like I need to get out.
Do you worry about having one of these episodes before you actually get into a slow elevator or a small locked room?

Yeah, I do a bit. If I see it’s one of those elevators, or a little storage room with no window and the door shuts tight, I start thinking about it before I go in. I know it’s not the same as being locked up, but my mind treats it like trouble right away.
Do you ever feel like you're having a heart attack or are going to pass out when you have one of these episodes?
I don’t really know about a heart attack. It feels scary in the moment, but I haven’t thought of it that way. Passing out… no, I don’t think I’ve felt like I was going to faint.
Do you think the fear of being in these small or locked spaces is what causes your chest to jump and the urge to escape?

Yes, I think so. It’s the small space or knowing I’m kind of stuck in there that sets it off. Like if I get in a slow elevator or a locked little room, my chest jumps right away and I just want to get back out before I can even think much.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt this intense fear or discomfort without being in a small or locked space?

No, not really. It’s when I step into a slow elevator or one of those small locked rooms that it hits me. My chest kind of jumps right away, and I feel like I need to get back out. Outside of that kind of space, I don’t think I’ve had it happen.
Do you often worry about everyday things, like work, finances, or your health, even when you're not in a situation that triggers your fear of small spaces?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things now and then, but it’s not something that goes on all the time. It’s mostly those small, closed-in places that get to me.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things like work, finances, or your health on a daily basis?
No, not on a daily basis. I mean, I have regular worries like anyone, but I don’t sit around worrying about work or money or my health all the time.
Is your fear only of the small or locked space itself, or is it also of having a panic attack or other symptoms while in those spaces?

It’s more the space itself, I think. Like, I know a little storage room or an elevator at the museum isn’t really the same as being locked up, but once I see there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind treats it like trouble right away.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things in your life when you are not in a situation that triggers your fear of small spaces?
Not really, no. I mean, I’ve got regular things on my mind like anybody does, but I don’t notice myself worrying too much unless I’m dealing with one of those tight little spaces.
Do you worry excessively about several different things in your life, not just the small or locked spaces?
No, I don’t think so. I worry about normal things now and then, but not several different things all the time. It’s mostly when I’m dealing with those small or closed-in places.
Is there anything else that you fear or avoid besides small or locked spaces?
No, not that I can think of. It’s really just those small, closed-in places that get to me.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most of the time, even when you're not in a small or locked space?

No, I wouldn’t say most of the time. If I’m just at home or out doing regular things, I’m usually alright. It’s more when I get near one of those small or locked-in spaces that I start feeling on edge.
Do you often find yourself anxious about various aspects of your daily life?
No, I haven’t noticed that. I don’t usually sit around worrying about all kinds of daily things.
